auraIntro: Explorer, Triangulum Galaxy is the third-largest member of our Local Group, renowned for giant starbirth nebula NGC 604.
overview: The Triangulum Galaxy (M33 or NGC 598) is a spiral galaxy roughly 2.73 million light-years from Earth in the constellation Triangulum.
formation: Formed approximately 12 billion years ago, M33 is gravitationally bound to the Andromeda Galaxy (M31) and undergoing intense localized starbirth.
structure: A unbarred spiral galaxy spanning 60,000 light-years in diameter. Intriguingly, spectroscopic analysis indicates M33 lacks a central supermassive black hole.
discoveryHistory: Discovered before 1654 by Giovanni Battista Hodierna and independently cataloged by Charles Messier in 1764.
observationTips: Under dark skies, M33 is one of the most distant permanent objects visible to the naked eye. Wide-field binoculars reveal its loose spiral arms.
funFacts: Contains NGC 604, one of the largest known H II star-forming regions in the Local Group, over 40 times larger than the Orion Nebula.
Lacks a central supermassive black hole, making it a critical laboratory for studying galaxy cores without SMBH feedback.
Orbiting the Andromeda Galaxy and scheduled for a potential gravitational encounter prior to the Milky Way merger.

cards.title: Nursery of Giant Stars
cards.subtitle: NGC 604 & Supermassive Black Hole Absence
cards.body: NGC 604 in M33 contains over 200 young high-mass stars in a nebula 1,500 light-years across. Unlike most spiral galaxies, M33 has no supermassive black hole at its center.
bulletPoints: NGC 604 is 40x larger than the Orion Nebula.
Upper limit on central black hole mass is under 3,000 solar masses.
Gravitationally tied to the larger Andromeda galaxy.
